description: SSAPy is a Python tool for modelling satellite orbits from low Earth orbit toward cislunar space. The JOSS paper describes orbit propagation with selectable gravitational, atmospheric, radiation and manoeuvre forces, plus observation and uncertainty functions. Its own repository identifies an MIT licence, so the code is free. Inputs include orbital elements or state vectors and satellite physical parameters. Outputs are predicted trajectories, state vectors and observability measures. Coverage is the orbital region and time period chosen for each run. Infrastructure modellers could use those paths when assessing satellite-positioning or communications service availability. That application requires a separate link or service model; SSAPy does not itself predict end-user outages. A caveat is that force models and uncertain initial state can cause trajectory errors to grow over time. No directly related catalogue record was confirmed. The package was not installed and no orbit was propagated. It supports simulation of orbital positions used as inputs to separate satellite service assessments.
inputs: Satellite mass, area, drag and force-model settings
name: SSAPy satellite orbit modelling package
